newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Moody's assigns Ba2 rating to Moscow Eurobonds.
newsitem.headline: Moody's assigns Ba2 rating to Moscow Eurobonds.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said on Monday it has assigned a Ba2 foreign-currency rating to the City of Moscow's forthcoming Eurobond issue.
Russian news agencies have reported the City of Moscow will issue its first $400 million Eurobond by March 15.
In a statement issued in Hong Kong, Moody's said this was the first time it had rated any debt of a territorial government in Russia.
The rating agency said the rating is constrained by the Russian Federation's existing Ba2 foreign-currency rating ceiling.

The assessment recognises the Moscow's position as one of the economically strongest regions in Russia, the city's highly autonomous status as a regional government of the Federation and its good track record in carrying out its responsibilities and in managing its vast resources, Moody's said.

Moody's said the rating also takes into account the inherent uncertainties related to the city's evolving administrative and budgetary structures and powers as well as to the relative fluidity still existing in the country as a whole.

"Due to the diversity of its economic base and to a rapidly expanding service sector, Moscow has suffered less from the economic downturn than other parts of the Federation," it said, adding that the lion's share of foreign investment is channelled to Moscow.
